# Pages

## index

### I build the systems between a measurement and a decision.

Data platform engineer in Munich. Specialized in scalable BI Solutions.

Projects

#### Now building

In active development

##### FX Macro Data Platform

A data platform for macroeconomic and FX time series, built so that every number can be traced back to what was knowable at the moment it was published.

Macro data gets revised. A GDP print or an inflation reading is published, then corrected — sometimes more than once, sometimes quietly. Keep only the latest value and you lose the version that mattered for a backtest, a research note or an audit. So the platform keeps every vintage: provider responses are stored untouched, and the warehouse records both the period a value describes and the day it became known.

- Raw data is immutable

- Every revision becomes a new vintage

- The warehouse rebuilds from raw

- Failures are loud, never silent

Every stage runs in its own Docker container

[View on GitHub](https://github.com/julianhilgemann/fx_macro_platform) [Why structure is the product](/story#structure)

#### What I do

One chain, three stages. A measurement has to land somewhere, be modelled into something that holds, and leave as a number someone can act on. I work across all three.

- **Platforms** Microsoft Fabric, run like a product. A multi-tenant setup where every customer gets their own Dev, Test and Prod on shared capacity. Changes go through source files, Git and DevOps, so an environment can be rebuilt rather than remembered. [How that runs today](/about#platform)

- **Data Warehousing** Modelled once, so it can be reused. Warehouses and lakehouses with real models: a named grain, declared relationships, and lineage you can walk from a dashboard figure back to its row. On Fabric today, on Postgres and dbt before that. [The case for structure](/story#structure)

- **Business Intelligence** The number people actually act on. Dashboards, forecasts and scenario planning, over a metric layer that holds still. A number is only worth acting on if you can say what it leaves out, so the definitions and the uncertainty travel with it. [Data products in fintech](/about#bi)

And then the same chain backwards — a number opened back up into colour, motion and sound. [That is the other half of the work.](/story#expansion)

#### Selected work

[All projects](/projects)

## story

### From signal to number, and back.

This page follows one signal from the world into a database, down to a single number, and back out as sound.

Everything I do with data is either compression or expansion. Compression to navigate, expansion to express. I build every stage of that chain, and the number in the middle is the narrowest point of it.

It starts as signal.

Signal

#### Reality has no sample rate.

Light, sound, pressure, faces: the world reaches you all at once, in continuous time, at a bandwidth nothing could store. It is denser than any instrument, any database and any brain can hold.

Noise is just signal you haven't modelled yet.

→

Belief

#### We don't see the world. We see our best current guess about it.

Perception is inference: a prior, updated by evidence, never the thing itself. Your brain doesn't record the signal. It guesses, and keeps correcting the guess.

Resolution: the image sharpens, the decision lands.

→

Measurement

#### To measure is to decide what to lose.

Every measurement picks a rate, a resolution and a blind spot. Data starts when someone decides what to write down — and, with it, what not to.

Every measure is a choice.

See the ingestion layer: FRED, ECB, Bundesbank →

Structure

#### A number means nothing outside the system that holds it.

Samples become tables, tables become models, models depend on each other. That graph is the real product. Hundreds of workspaces, thousands of objects, one lineage that has to hold across Dev, Test and Prod.

Tables. Models. Dependencies.

See the platform →

Inference

#### A forecast is perception pointed at the future.

With enough structure, the past makes testable claims about what we haven't seen. The curve from the second chapter comes back here as the fan around the line: same shape, now pointed forward.

Then, a forecast.

See the forecasting work →

Number

#### Everything collapses into one number. This is where most people think data ends.

A KPI is a whole system compressed until someone can act on it. Every stage so far is underneath it, and none of it is visible.

One number.

See the dashboard years →

Expansion

#### A number can be opened up again, into something you feel.

Run the pipeline backwards: the number drives frequency, motion and light. The noise from the first chapter is back, and this time it has rhythm.

The last bar of the chart is the first bar of the track.

See what comes out →

#### Compression to navigate. Expansion to express.

I build in both directions: the systems that turn the world into numbers, and the pieces that turn numbers back into something you can hear.

It ends as signal.

Projects

About

Contact

## about

### About

Hi, I'm Julian, a data platform engineer with a passion for all things data. Originally from Berlin, I'm now based in Munich, where I work as a BI engineer at a German fintech that builds financial reporting for small and mid-sized businesses. What I enjoy most is the whole journey data takes: from the stochastic origins of an observation, through measurement and storage, transformation and aggregation, to communicating what it means and the real-world actions it drives. I also see data as a medium for creative expression: through sound and visuals, those samples of reality can carry meaning that reaches people on an emotional level. Below are a few data points to get to know me. If you'd like to get in touch, reach out or connect with me on LinkedIn.

LinkedIn

#### The path so far

##### Multi-tenant Fabric product

I work remotely from Munich as a contributor on the product team behind a multi-tenant analytics product on Microsoft Fabric. One large semantic model serves many customers, each with their own Dev, Test and Prod workspaces, all running on shared Fabric capacity. On shared capacity a slow measure is everyone's problem, so the work is about scale: DAX measures that stay fast as the model grows, data pipelines and APIs that feed it, and data apps built on top. Most of it I build agentically, with coding agents working on the model's source files and Git behind every change.

##### Data products in fintech

Before that I built data products inside a fintech in Munich, end to end: gathering the requirements, building the warehouse, and putting Power BI dashboards on top. Postgres and dbt underneath, Power BI on Fabric and Azure, and Excel wherever finance needed it. The other half of the job was finance itself: revenue forecasting, scenario planning, KPI reporting, financial modelling and M&amp;A due diligence, plus the stakeholder work of agreeing what a number means before anyone builds it.

##### Graduate studies in Quantitative Economics

At Christian-Albrechts University Kiel, focused on time series econometrics and foreign exchange markets. I left the programme for work in Munich. The interest in FX stayed: it is what the FX Macro Data Platform is built around.

##### Insurance and real estate

Work in insurance and real estate in Berlin, between the two degrees.

##### Bachelor's in Business Administration

At Technical University Brandenburg. My thesis was in multivariate macroeconometric forecasting: which macroeconomic aggregates hold up as forecasters of inflation against ARMA and VARMA benchmarks, as a way into how monetary policy reaches prices. That is where the time series started.

##### Audio engineering and music production

Before university I was deep into audio engineering and digital music production in Ableton Live. That is where signal processing started for me: sampling, filters, EQ, compression. It came back later in time series econometrics, where a moving average is a low-pass filter and a business cycle is a frequency band. Same mathematics, different signal.

##### Abitur at a German school abroad

Germany's university-entrance qualification, taken at a German school in Moscow and taught to the Baden-Württemberg curriculum.

##### School, with a focus on art

I grew up in Berlin and went to the Kurt-Schwitters-Oberschule, where my focus was art, until the move to Moscow.

#### How I work

- **Clarity before code.** Architecture follows from a clear picture of what the product is for, not the other way around.

- **Craft in the details.** Correct isn't enough. Naming, layout, load times and edge cases decide whether people come back.

- **Impact you can see.** A dashboard nobody opens is a failed project, however elegant the model.

#### Technologies I use

I enjoy an AI-forward way of working. I combine the tools below with agentic workflows, and together they act as a kind of brush: a way to turn technical ideas into working systems quickly, and to separate signal from noise along the way.

#### Questions? I reply fast.

Contact me

## services

#### Let’s design your decision system.

If your company has data but decisions still rely on gut feeling, we should talk.

Schedule Consultation

#### Pricing model

Fixed-price configurator. All prices net, plus VAT. Quote valid 30 days. Price list version 2026-08-01. Entry point: from EUR 6,000.

##### Foundation & Fabric workspace setup

EUR 2,400, mandatory.

- Workspace and capacity configuration
- Dev / test / prod environments + deployment pipeline
- Git integration and naming/governance conventions
- Kickoff and requirements session

##### Quantity-based items

**Data connections** (per source, 1-25); volume tapering applies.

- Standard connector (SQL, SharePoint, Excel/CSV, common SaaS): EUR 600
- Custom REST API (OAuth, pagination, rate limits): EUR 1,200
- Legacy / undocumented / manual file-based: EUR 2,100

**Report pages** (per page, 1-40); volume tapering applies.

- Standard (visuals on an existing model): EUR 450
- Interactive (drill-through, bookmarks, what-if, dynamic measures): EUR 800
- Advanced (custom visuals, complex layout, heavy DAX): EUR 1,300

##### Scope options

**Semantic model** (required)

- Compact — up to ~5 tables, standard measures: EUR 1,800
- Standard — up to ~15 tables, time intelligence, calculation groups: EUR 3,600
- Complex — multi-fact, advanced DAX patterns, reconciliation logic: EUR 6,500

**Upstream data transformation**

- None — data is already prepared: EUR 0
- Light — cleaning, conformed dimensions, a handful of views/notebooks: EUR 2,400
- Standard — medallion lakehouse, incremental loads, historization, orchestration: EUR 6,000
- Advanced — SCD2, reconciliation, multi-currency / IFRS-style calculation layers: EUR 12,000

##### Modules

**Design system & theming**

- Default theme: EUR 0
- Branded theme — theme file, colors/fonts/logo, page templates: EUR 1,200
- Full design system — tokenized theme, component & layout library, documentation: EUR 3,500

**AI readiness** — included as standard (list value EUR 2,900)

- Metadata layer: semantic descriptions, business glossary, model documentation
- Agentic enablement: skill files, curated query patterns, agent-consumable model contracts

**Onboarding & enablement**

- Handover — recorded walkthrough + documentation: EUR 0
- Team training — live 2h session + materials: EUR 900

##### Complexity factors (combined cap 1.6x)

- Multiple tenants or distinct audiences: +20%
- Row-level security required: +10%
- Multi-language reporting: +15%

##### Ongoing support (minimum 12 months)

- **Reactive support** — EUR 290/month: Bug fixes; Response target 2 business days; Up to 2h/month
- **Managed** — EUR 690/month: Everything in Reactive; Refresh monitoring & proactive checks; Up to 4h/month
- **Partnership** — EUR 1,400/month: Everything in Managed; 8h/month change budget; Quarterly review

##### Custom work

Custom work & change budget at EUR 110/hour.

Prepaid blocks: 10h EUR 1,100, 25h EUR 2,600 (5% off), 50h EUR 4,950 (10% off).

##### Not included

- Microsoft Fabric capacity (F-SKU) and Power BI licences — billed by Microsoft directly to the client
- Third-party data source subscription costs
- Travel, if on-site work is requested
